The case is decided as auto-fix, and the coder takes it from here.

I first sent it to investigation, because the runbook gives different decisions depending on what the cause turns out to be. The investigator found the cause in `GetOrderTotal` in `src/OrderService/Api/OrderTotal.cs`, line 18. The method reads `DiscountRates[order.DiscountCode]` without checking the key. Order 1003 carries the retired code `SUMMER25`, which is not in the table (only `WELCOME10` and `VIP20` are), so the lookup throws `KeyNotFoundException`. The investigator rated this as area code with high confidence, and I checked that the run records the same finding.

That matches the Decisions row "a crash in this method's code, its cause certain, e.g. a `KeyNotFoundException` for a retired discount code", which is auto-fix for the coder. The fix is to give no discount for an unknown code, so `WELCOME10`, `VIP20` and no-code totals stay the same.

I could not brief the coder myself, because it is not on the list of agents I may ask. The auto-fix decision is recorded so that the coder can pick it up. The investigator did not run the tests or read order 1003's record.
